title: Do plumbing and drainage work to the plumbing code (NCC Volume Three)
what: Have plumbing and sanitary drainage plans approved by a certifier, who may approve them only if the work complies with the plumbing code: the Plumbing Code of Australia (NCC Volume Three) with the ACT Appendix. The edition in force is NCC 2025 since 1 May 2026, with a 12-month transition. The ACT's variations are in the ACT Appendix on the ACT Legislation Register, not counted here.

sources.title: Water and Sewerage Act 2000 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 8(2) (current republication (R29, from 26 November 2025; Water and Sewerage Act 2000 | Acts))
sources.quote: (2) A certifier must not issue a plan approval unless— (a) the application is in accordance with section 7 (Application for plan approval); and (b) the plan that accompanies the application complies with any requirements prescribed by regulation; and (c) the applicant has obtained the approvals mentioned in subsection (1); and (d) the requirements of this Act have otherwise been complied with; and (e) the proposed plumbing or sanitary drainage work complies with the plumbing code.

sources.title: Water and Sewerage Act 2000 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 44C(1) (current republication (R29, from 26 November 2025; Water and Sewerage Act 2000 | Acts))
sources.quote: plumbing code means— (a) the Plumbing Code of Australia prepared and published by the Australian Building Codes Board as amended from time to time by— (i) the Australian Building Codes Board; and (ii) the Australian Capital Territory Appendix to the Plumbing Code of Australia; and (b) a document prescribed by regulation.

confidence_note: The law's own words require building or plumbing work to comply with the code. Drafted on 27 November 2026 for the NCC work (docs/plan_ncc_ingestion.md, phase N3); the variation counts are from the NCC 2025 dataset.

assessment.summary: Work must meet the National Construction Code (Volume Three, the Plumbing Code of Australia) as the ACT applies it. The code sets minimum safety, health, amenity, accessibility and energy standards, whose benefits are not weighed here; meeting and certifying them adds to the cost of every project.

marks.reason: Designing, documenting and certifying each project against the code adds cost, and the state's own variations add to it for builders who work in several states.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked to agree with the NCC adoption records (burden -1); the Productivity Commission finds several code changes were adopted although their impact analyses showed a net cost. No evaluation of the requirement itself was found.
